extensions.scope: Governs the web edition (src/Mazesta.App/wwwroot) only. The WPF edition (src/Mazesta.Desktop, Themes/Dark.xaml) is a separate earlier design in the same brand colours and is not governed by this file.

display-numeral.purpose: Giant live temperatures on the poster plane; rolls digit by digit.

headline-page.purpose: One page title per page, over a 2px paper rule.

headline-verdict.purpose: The machine's standing on the dashboard plane.

value.purpose: Every sensor reading, unit, model name: Latin, tabular, isolated LTR.

figure.purpose: Benchmark metrics and the tuning live strip.

index-number.purpose: Persian two-digit index and queue step numbers.

shadows.name: toast-lift
shadows.purpose: Transient toasts only; the rest of the system is flat.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single house easing for every transition and entrance.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Index underline draw, switch knob, slab arrow.

motion.name: roll
motion.purpose: Rolling numerals: each changed digit column slides to its value.

motion.name: view-transition-new
motion.purpose: Incoming page wipes in along the grid (skipped when hidden, under reduced motion or with ?still).

motion.name: rule-in
motion.purpose: Columns, page heads and section heads.

motion.name: range-rule
motion.purpose: Min/max span and current tick glide.

motion.name: progress
motion.purpose: Progress bars grow from the reading-start edge.

motion.name: motion-off
motion.purpose: Removes all animations, transitions and view-transition animations.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Below: monitoring and tuning splits stack; tuning live strip goes from 6 to 3 columns.

breakpoints.name: min-window
breakpoints.purpose: Smallest window the app allows; dashboard part columns stay one row.

narrative.overview:
The machine's state is set as an Iranian-modernist poster on a strict grid. Type, flat planes and hairline rules do all the work: brand yellow arrives as whole planes, never as an accent sprinkled on controls; the ground is ink black; type and rules are paper off-white. The category's rounded card dashboard with gauges and glow is refused. There are no corners, no cards, and almost no shadows. Hierarchy comes from weight and scale alone: a heavy Persian face for words, a condensed grotesk for numerals, and giant temperature figures that roll to their live values.

The page reads right to left first, with every Latin value isolated left to right and kept in Latin digits. Density is poster-like at the top (one yellow plane, two giant numerals) and dense beneath (ruled columns of tabular figures). Honesty is visible: a value that was not measured is drawn as a diagonal hatch with the words "not available", never as a zero.
keyCharacteristics: Yellow (#fdd400) as whole planes: the dashboard's hero plane, the current index item, primary buttons; a part's own page lays its plane in the part's hue.
One part, one hue, everywhere: CPU blue, GPU violet, RAM cyan, storage orange, network pink, board sand; no part hue is green or red.
Panels (14px radius) box every part: a hue strip, a hue wash, a short summary and details folded under a chevron.
A numbered index (Persian two-digit numbers) on the reading-start edge as navigation; Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+0 open the first ten.
Registration crosses at the four corners of every plane.
State colour laws: green only for passed, red only for failed, the hatch only for not measured.
Motion is typographic: rolling numerals, a plane wipe between pages, panels rising in. All of it switches off under reduced motion or `?still`.

rules.name: The One Part, One Hue Rule
rules.body: A part never changes colour between pages, and no two parts share one. The hue is set once per container (.p-cpu sets --hue) and everything inside reads var(--hue); the canvas and the WPF overlay use the same values.

rules.name: The Whole Plane Rule
rules.body: Yellow is laid down as a plane or a full-row fill. It is never a glow, a gradient border or a tinted card.

rules.name: The State Law Rule
rules.body: Green means passed and nothing else; red means failed and nothing else; the diagonal hatch means not measured and always carries the words. A test that did not run gets `pill-none` or amber, never green.

rules.name: The Missing Is Drawn Rule
rules.body: An unavailable value renders as the hatch (135deg paper lines at 22% on ink, ink lines at 28% on yellow, 1px every 6px) with the localized "not available" text. Never 0, never a dash.

rules.name: The Latin Island Rule
rules.body: Every value, unit, model name, version or path is wrapped in the `lat` or `num` role: Archivo, `direction: ltr`, `unicode-bidi: isolate`, tabular figures. Persian digits are reserved for indices, dates and prose.

rules.name: The Weight Is Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Headings differ by weight and size only. No colour, no underline accents, no uppercase eyebrows above headlines.

rules.name: The Reading-Start Rule
rules.body: Layout uses logical properties (`inline-start`, `inline-end`) so the index, rules and fills follow `dir`. Latin values align left inside their isolated run.

rules.name: The Quiet Box Rule
rules.body: A panel is separated by its hue (strip, 38% border, 15% wash) and one soft under-shadow, never by glow, blur or a second shadow.

dos: Do lay yellow (#fdd400) down as a whole plane or a full-width bar, with ink (#0c0c0c) type on it.
Do put every value in the Latin role (Archivo, tabular, isolated LTR) and every heading in Vazirmatn at 800–900.
Do draw a missing value as the hatch with the words "not available".
Do separate content with rules: 1px hairlines between rows, a 2px paper rule on top of a column or page head.
Do use logical properties so the index, fills and underlines start at the reading-start edge in both RTL and LTR.
Do keep motion on opacity, transform and clip-path, and honour reduced motion and `?still`.
donts: Don't use green for anything but a passed result, or red for anything but a failed one.
Don't show 0, a dash or a placeholder for an unmeasured value.
Don't build rounded cards, gauges, glows or drop shadows; the toast is the only lifted surface.
Don't set Latin figures in Vazirmatn or let them render as Persian digits.
Don't add uppercase letter-spaced eyebrows or kickers above headlines; the plane's shop and date sit in a colophon at its foot.
Don't animate while the window is hidden or add timers that wake without need.
